questions.question: If 4th January, 2008 falls on Friday, what day of week will fall on 4th January, 2009?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

If the 1st day of any non-leap year (Eg. 1st Jan 2022) is on Friday then 8th day, 15th day, 22nd day, 29th day ....... 365th day will be on Friday only. 

Therefore, the last day will be the same day for a non-leap year.

For a leap year, the last day will be the next day that comes after the first day as we have one extra day i.e. 366 days.

__**Calculation:**__

__**Given:**__

4th January 2008 falls on Friday, ∴ 1st January 2008 will be on Tuesday and 31st December 2008 falls on Wednesday.

As per the given condition, 1st January 2009 will be on Thursday and 4th January will be on Sunday.

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All breads are meat

**Conclusions:**

I. Some beans are breads.

II. Some breads are beans.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.

1) We have to check the conclusions are 100% match with the statement. If the conclusion is 100% match with the given statement then the conclusion is true. If there is a 1% chance of not following the statement then the conclusion is considered to be false.

2) The possibility case can be considered to be "false" in "definite case".

3) In Possibility case, either "can" or "possible" word must be present.

Conclusion II: Some breads are beans → False (This is possible but not definite)

1. The elements should be the same in both the statements.

2. Individually both the conclusions should be false.

questions.question: The sum of the present ages of a mother and a son is 50 years. 4 years ago, the ratio of their ages was 6 : 1. Find the current age of the mother.
questions.solution:
4 years ago, the ratio of their ages was 6 : 1.

Let their ages be measured in terms of unit x.

So, presents the age of a mother is 6x + 4 and the present age of a son is x + 4.

The sum of the present ages of a mother and a son is 50 years.

According to problem:

(6x + 4) + (x + 4) = 50

⇒ 6x + 4 + x + 4 = 50

⇒ 7x = 50 – 8

⇒ 7x = 42

⇒ x = 6

So, the present age of mother is 6x + 4 i.e, (6 × 6) + 4 = 40 years.

Hence, 40 years is the correct answer.

questions.question: In sweet pea, the tendrils are modified
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Leaflets**

__**Explanation**__

In sweet pea (Lathyrus odoratus), the tendrils are modified leaflets. Let's break down why this is the correct answer by understanding the structure and function of tendrils in sweet peas.

Understanding Tendrils

Tendrils are specialized structures that help climbing plants attach to and climb up supports. They are typically slender, coiled structures that can wrap around objects for stability.

Types of Tendrils

Tendrils can arise from different parts of the plant, including:

**Stem branches:** In some plants, tendrils can be modified branches.

**Leaflets:** In many legumes, tendrils are modified leaflets, which are the individual segments of a compound leaf.

**Leaves:** Some plants have tendrils that are modified whole leaves.

**Stipules: **These are small, leaf-like appendages at the base of leaf stalks in some plants, but tendrils are rarely modifications of stipules.

It de-reserved several industries previously earmarked for the public sector.
It banned FDI in manufacturing and core industries.
It expanded the scope of licensing for all industries.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It de-reserved several industries previously earmarked for the public sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **New Industrial Policy (NIP) of 1991** aimed to liberalize the Indian economy and reduce government intervention in industries.
 
• It removed many industries from the list exclusively reserved for the **public sector**, allowing private entities to enter these sectors.
 
• **De-reservation** enabled industries such as **steel, air transport, and telecommunications** to attract private investments and improve competitiveness.
 
• This move was part of broader **economic reforms**, including **disinvestment** and the promotion of a market-driven economy.
 
• The focus was on reducing the monopoly of the public sector and encouraging **foreign direct investment (FDI)** and private sector participation.
 
• The policy also introduced measures to ensure efficient allocation of resources, technology upgrades, and the adoption of global best practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: Five-year industrial licensing review mechanism**__

 __
 
• The **Industrial Licensing system** was significantly abolished under the 1991 policy. It did not introduce a five-year licensing review mechanism but rather reduced licensing requirements for most industries.
 
• The removal of licensing barriers encouraged **entrepreneurship and industrial growth**.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Ban on FDI in manufacturing and core industries**__
 __
 
• The 1991 policy actually promoted **FDI** in various sectors, including manufacturing and core industries, to attract foreign capital and expertise.
 
• FDI limits were liberalized, and automatic approvals were introduced for several sectors.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Expanded scope of licensing for all industries**__
 
 
• The policy reduced the scope of licensing rather than expanding it. Licensing was retained only for a few strategic industries such as **defense and hazardous chemicals**.
 
• This was part of the move toward liberalization and a more open economy.

questions.question: Right to livelihood has been established as a part of which particular fundamental right by the Supreme Court?
questions.solution:
Right to livelihood has been established as a part of __**Right to life**__ by the Supreme Court. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Supreme Court of India has held that the right to livelihood is an integral part of the right to life, which is guaranteed under **Article 21 **of the Constitution. 
 
• This means that the government cannot deprive a person of their livelihood without a valid reason.
 
• The right to livelihood was first recognized as an inherent part of the right to life in the **case of Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985). **
 
• In this case, the Supreme Court ruled that the government could not evict pavement dwellers without providing them with alternative accommodation, as this would deprive them of their livelihood.
 
• The right to livelihood has been further affirmed in a number of other cases, including:
 
 
• **​In People's Union for Democratic Rights v. Union of India (1982), the Supreme Court held that the right to livelihood includes the right to work, the right to education, and the right to health.**
 
• **In Narmada Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2000), the Supreme Court held that the right to livelihood is a fundamental right that must be protected by the government.**
 
• **In Right to Food Campaign v. Union of India (2001), the Supreme Court held that the government has a duty to provide food to all its citizens, as this is essential for their right to livelihood.**
 
 
 
• The right to livelihood is an important right that ensures that all people have the opportunity to earn a living and support themselves and their families. 
 
• 
 
It is a right that is essential for human dignity and well-being.

 

Therefore the correct answer is** Right to life.**

questions.question: According to the Regulating Act 1773, which of the following options is INCORRECT about the powers and responsibilities of the Governor General?

options.text: Can make rules and regulations for the civil government of Fort William
Can control the presidencies of Madras and Bombay in war and peace
Powered to superintendent the presidencies of Madras and Bombay in war and peace
Can override the decision of his council

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Can override the decision of his council**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Regulating Act of 1773 established the office of the Governor-General of Bengal, who was assisted by an executive council of four members.
 
• The Governor-General was empowered to make rules and regulations for the civil government of Fort William in Bengal.
 
• The Governor-General had the power to control and superintend the presidencies of Madras and Bombay in matters of war and peace.
 
• However, the Governor-General could not override the decision of his council; decisions were to be taken collectively, and in the event of a tie, the Governor-General held the casting vote.
 
• This limitation was an attempt to ensure checks and balances within the colonial administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regulating Act of 1773:**

 
 
• The first attempt by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company and its territories in India.
 
• It marked the beginning of parliamentary control over the Company's administration in India.
 
• It restricted the private trade of Company officials and sought to address administrative corruption.
 
 
 
• **Governor-General of Bengal:**
 
 
• The Regulating Act designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal.
 
• Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General under the Act.
 
 
 
• **Executive Council:**
 
 
• The Governor-General's Executive Council consisted of four members appointed by the Court of Directors of the East India Company.
 
• It functioned as a decision-making body, with the Governor-General having the casting vote.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of the Regulating Act:**
 
 
• The Act failed to provide adequate checks on the Governor-General's powers.
 
• Conflicts often arose between the Governor-General and his council members due to the lack of clarity in decision-making authority.
 
• This led to the enactment of the Pitt's India Act of 1784, which introduced further reforms.

• A gerund is a verb that’s acting as a noun. 
 
• The verb—the word that describes the action that’s happening, like “reading,” “riding"—becomes a thing, a concept.
 
• It doesn’t stop being a verb, but the role it plays in a sentence shifts from describing the action to being the main point of the sentence.
 
 
• Example: She said that she used to enjoy skiing a lot when she was a kid.
 
 
 
• Gerunds are verbs in the present participle form. This means they’re the root verb + “ing”: apologizing, running, drinking.
 
• Now, in the given sentence, the correct word, that will act as a gerund in the sentence is "speeding."
 
• Thus, the correct sentence will be: The police arrested him for **speeding__**.
 
• Thus, the verb "speeding" is acting as a noun in the given sentence.
